userStories.title: Expose width-aware safe surface measurements
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Make plain input, ask and picker measurement describe the complete safe surface actually drawn at the current width.

**Motivation** — Independent mounted-frame probes find overflow on very short terminals even with no pending messages.

**Approach** — Extend the existing pure inputRows, askCardLayout and pickerLayout/pickerRows models with pure minimum/desired sizing helpers that the allocator can consume; keep measurement owned by each component rather than copying component constants into ChatApp. The spec requires: 'Surface minima and desired sizes come from pure component measurement helpers, not duplicated constants in ChatApp.' 'Measurement must include the actual input hint, width, busy state and text-row cap used for drawing.'

The safe minima at actual width are:
- Plain input: two rules plus one text row (three rows).
- Picker: its existing fixed frame/title/filter/note rows plus one selected-entry row for a nonempty filtered list. An empty list needs just those fixed rows and cannot choose or stop an entry. Extra entry rows yield down to this minimum.
- Approval/choice ask: top rule, the complete wrapped title/attribution, all rendered option rows, countdown and bottom rule. If command/reason/diff/summary body rows are withheld, also reserve the existing measured elision marker. No option/shortcut may remain actionable while its option row is clipped.
- Question ask: top rule, complete wrapped title, at least the first question-text row, the three-row minimum answer box, countdown and bottom rule; include the measured elision marker if more question text is withheld. Extra answer/body rows yield to this minimum. A blank question retains its empty text row.

'For ask/picker surfaces use the same ordering with input menus/previews absent; their desired extra body/list/answer rows occupy the same priority slot as extra input text rows.' 'These are sizing minima, not permission changes; existing elision semantics and option labels remain.' Keep the elision marker's own wrapped height in the model. Ensure the measured minimum can actually be drawn without losing title, actionable options, countdown, rules or minimum answer content. At insufficient budgets the model must let the frame allocator choose diagnostic rather than pretending an independently clamped surface is safe.

**Scope** — In: component-owned pure measurements and matching input/ask/picker drawing; parameterized pure/mounted assertions for wrapped titles/options, elision markers, actual hints and empty filtered pickers. Out: whole-frame allocation/pending projection (US-002), ChatApp suspension/composition (US-003), screen-wide key gating and hit tests (US-004); permission-policy changes.

**Interface** — The spec mandates no TypeScript signatures. Preserve existing layout helper entry points where practical and expose typed pure measurements containing safe minimum and desired sizes, including render-cap information sufficient for the allocator. Downstream stories must consume these measurements rather than recalculate component internals.

**Test strategy detail** — Write failing cases first in existing chat-input, ask-card, choice-card and picker UI suites, using pure layout helpers and mounted row-count comparisons at actual supported widths. Exercise narrow wrapped titles/attribution/options and wrapped elision markers, minimum/desired budgets, nonempty/empty filtered model lists and blank questions; retain existing labels and controller effects. Use shared helpers/fake clocks, not provider calls.
acceptanceCriteria: When plain-input measurement is requested at its minimum, then it reports three rows comprising two rules and one text row.
When inputRows() measures the draft and ChatInput's actual width, stdout-derived container width, hint, busy state and text-row cap, then its result equals the mounted input's physical row count.
When a nonempty filtered picker is measured at its safe minimum, then pickerLayout() draws its fixed frame/title/filter/note rows and one selected-entry row.
When a filtered picker list is empty, then its safe minimum contains only its existing fixed frame/title/filter/note rows.
When an empty filtered picker receives choose, cycle or stop input, then it invokes no entry action.
When an approval or choice ask is drawn at its measured minimum, then every wrapped title/attribution and option row remains visible alongside the top rule, countdown and bottom rule.
When approval/choice body rows are withheld, then the measured and drawn minimum includes the existing elision marker at its actual wrapped height.
When a question ask is drawn at its measured minimum, then it retains the complete wrapped title, first question-text row, three-row answer box, countdown and enclosing rules.
When additional question text is withheld, then its safe minimum includes the measured existing elision marker.
When a blank question is measured and drawn, then its empty question-text row remains present.

When an ask's optional body is elided, then the marker reports the exact number of withheld physical content rows using its existing label wording, preserving existing elision semantics and option labels.
When a focused empty busy input is drawn, then its inverse cursor remains immediately after the prompt marker without placeholder text, preserving the existing focused input regression behavior.
When a focused nonempty input with cursor index 1 draws the draft 'abc', then its inverse cursor covers 'b', preserving existing cursor placement.

routing.reasoning: Reuses three existing pure component layout models but must reconcile wrapped titles/options, elision and editor caps; lite isolation is sufficient because this story changes measurement/drawing, not authorization or permission enforcement.

userStories.title: Allocate one bounded frame and combined pending preview projection
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Introduce one pure deterministic frame allocator and one height-aware combined steering/queue preview projection.

**Motivation** — Seventeen unresolved accepted steers overflow an 80x24 frame even without resizing.

**Approach** — Create a small pure frame-layout module, not more arithmetic in ChatApp. Consume US-001 component measurements. 'For terminal height H >= 2, the rendered frame must use no more than H - 1 physical rows, preserving the existing one-row slack. At H = 1, render at most one non-interactive clipped diagnostic row; no scrolling output. Keep existing fallback dimensions for unavailable/zero terminal dimensions.' 'Allocate nonnegative integer row counts once and use the same result to render every region and compute viewport top, footer location, visible menus and their key ownership. No independent minimum may increase the sum beyond the usable budget.'

'Its result must identify the actually visible surface (`input`, `ask`, `picker`, or `diagnostic`), each region’s row count and top coordinate, and which keyboard/mouse targets are active within those bounds.' Include header sections, transcript, status row, each explicit status gap, combined previews, surface, menus and footer. Resolve ask > picker > input precedence before allocating; overlays have zero preview/menu shares. Use zero-based region top coordinates, converting only at 1-based terminal-event boundaries. Lock/precedence inputs and actual visibility must constrain returned targets.

Apply the spec algorithm verbatim: 'The essential set is the current input/overlay minimum, one footer row, and exactly one live status row whenever the existing working-line predicate is true. The live status row is never sacrificed in an interactive layout; diagnostic fallback replaces the whole layout if that essential set cannot fit. Its two gaps are optional and distinct from that row.'

'For the input surface, begin with the essential set plus the normal three-row header, one transcript row, desired extra input text rows up to the existing editor cap, desired slash/mention rows up to their existing caps, up to four combined preview rows, and the pair of working gaps when busy. If this exceeds usable rows, reduce in this exact order: (1) remove both working gaps, (2) reduce preview rows down to zero, (3) reduce menu rows down to zero, (4) reduce extra input text rows down to zero, leaving its three-row framed minimum, (5) remove the header path and rule together, (6) remove the remaining header row, (7) remove the one reserved transcript row. Thus input text outranks menus, menus outrank previews, previews have no guaranteed minimum, and the gaps yield first. Give any remaining space to the transcript. Recompute from desired sizes on every resize; never persist the degraded counts as desired state.'

'For ask/picker surfaces use the same ordering with input menus/previews absent; their desired extra body/list/answer rows occupy the same priority slot as extra input text rows.' 'If the essential set still exceeds usable rows after the optional regions yield, replace the interactive frame with a height-bounded `Terminal too small — enlarge to continue` diagnostic (clipped to the supported width). This applies to any undersized input or overlay, not just a fixed terminal-height threshold.' All diagnostic surface targets are inactive. Working gaps have either one row on each side or zero on both sides; no live status means zero rows for all three parts.

Implement combined pending projection in message-queue.ts using the allocated preview rows: 'Steering and queue previews share one height budget; adding separate fixed caps alone is not sufficient for short terminals. Keep the existing group order: pending steers in arrival order, then queued messages oldest first.' 'Use a normal maximum of four combined preview rows. If all pending items fit, show all of them. Otherwise reserve the final available preview row for `+N pending`, with N equal to all pending items not individually shown across both groups. With one row available and more than one pending item, show only that summary; a single pending item fits and shows its labeled preview. With zero rows, draw nothing and reserve nothing. Each visible item keeps its `steering` or `queued` label. Summary counts items, not text lines. Sanitize/flatten preview text as today and fit each to one physical row.'

'This is only a projection. Do not truncate stored messages, mutate queue order, resolve steering promises, or change sending/draining on resize.' Keep the storage/settlement helpers unchanged.

**Scope** — In: frame-layout pure API, combined projection and boundary/order/count tests. Preserve current helper entry points until US-003 migrates their callers; US-003 removes or delegates obsolete competing bottom-region arithmetic. Out: ChatApp rendering/state suspension and caller migration (US-003), event-consumer/renderer integration (US-004), queue draining, and changes to accepted/discarded steering behavior.

**Interface** — No signatures were prescribed by the spec. Use a typed options-object API named allocateChatFrame() in frame-layout.ts and a pure pendingPreviewLines() projection in message-queue.ts. The immutable allocation result is the sole final geometry/visibility model, not a second budget computed inside hooks. Component helpers supply minimum/desired dimensions and rendering caps.

**Test strategy detail** — Write pure table-driven boundary tests for H=1,4,5,8,9,10,12,24,40, idle/busy, short/long drafts, menus, queue-only/steer-only/mixed items, asks and pickers. Assert sums, integers, nonnegative regions, cumulative coordinates, precedence, diagnostic target inactivity and exact degradation order. Cross 0,1,4,5,17,40 pending items with budgets 0..4; assert exact ordered text/counts and unchanged input arrays. Keep these mandatory without PTY capabilities.
acceptanceCriteria: When allocateChatFrame() receives any height in 2, 3, 4, 5, 8, 9, 10, 12, 24 and 40 across idle/busy, short/long drafts, queue-only, steer-only, mixed pending items, menus, asks and pickers, then the total allocated physical rows are at most H - 1.
When allocateChatFrame() receives any height in 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 8, 9, 10, 12, 24 and 40 across the surface matrix, then every region allocation is a nonnegative integer.
When allocateChatFrame() returns an interactive layout, then each region's top coordinate equals the cumulative allocated rows preceding it in the drawn composition.
When allocateChatFrame() returns diagnostic, then every keyboard/mouse surface target in its result is inactive.
When H equals 1, then allocateChatFrame() selects diagnostic with at most one row and no active surface targets.

When optional input regions exceed usable rows, then allocateChatFrame() reduces them in the specified order: gap pair, previews, menus, extra input text, header path/rule pair, remaining header row, reserved transcript row.
When an ask or picker owns the surface, then allocateChatFrame() assigns zero rows to input menus and pending previews.
When both ask and picker are present, then allocateChatFrame() selects ask as the visible surface.
When the essential surface minimum plus footer and required live status row cannot fit, then allocateChatFrame() selects diagnostic instead of an actionable clipped surface.
When a live working line is present in an interactive allocation, then exactly one status row is reserved.
When working gaps yield under pressure, then the returned before/after gap counts are both zero rather than one-sided.
When no live working line exists, then the allocation reserves neither status row nor gaps.
When terminal space becomes available again, then allocateChatFrame() derives region sizes from desired sizes rather than retaining degraded counts.

When pendingPreviewLines() receives N=0,1,4,5,17 or 40 pending items and budget B=0..4, then its output length equals min(N,B), including the overflow summary inside that budget rather than beside it.
When N pending items exceed a preview budget B in 1..4, then pendingPreviewLines() individually shows the first B-1 items and the summary count equals N-B+1 across both groups.
When all pending items fit the preview budget, then pendingPreviewLines() returns every item with its steering or queued label in steer-arrival order followed by queue-oldest-first order.
When pending items exceed a positive preview budget, then the final available preview row is '+N pending' where N counts every item not individually shown across both groups.
When one preview row is available for more than one item, then pendingPreviewLines() returns only the combined summary.
When one preview row is available for one item, then pendingPreviewLines() returns that item's labeled preview.
When zero preview rows are available, then pendingPreviewLines() returns no rows.
When preview text contains line breaks or terminal escapes, then each projected item remains sanitized and fitted to one physical row at the supported width.
When pendingPreviewLines() projects hidden items, then the complete stored messages, queue order and steering promises remain unchanged.

routing.reasoning: Introduces a pure allocation abstraction spanning measured surfaces, degradation priorities, coordinates and a shared projection; no permission or host execution decisions are modified.

userStories.title: Render bounded frames with status gaps and persistent hidden state
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Replace ChatApp's independent height floors with the allocation result and preserve the current chat state through compact and diagnostic layouts.

**Motivation** — Start a turn, queue four messages, resize 80x24 -> 80x12 -> 80x24: the header scrolls out at the smaller size and stale transcript/status text remains after expansion and clock ticks.

**Approach** — Measure desired content at the actual width with US-001 helpers, call US-002's allocator once per frame and draw every region from that returned geometry. Preserve normal composition: header, transcript, padded live status when present, pending previews, bottom input/overlay, footer. Use ask > picker > input precedence and zero preview/menu rows for overlays. Remove/delegate the old bottomBudget/inputBudget/viewport minimum arithmetic rather than running two models. As part of this render integration, separate useMentionMenu's desired row demand from its final allocated view: the current budget/shareOf calculation cannot determine demand after degradation. Derive slash and mention desired rows from their existing content models/caps without a terminal-height budget, then project the drawn view using only the allocator's final menu share. Preserve query/list/pointer refs. US-004 consumes that final visibility for event-time ownership; it does not provide a missing measurement dependency for this story. The actual hint, busy value, width/container and editor cap used in measurement must be the drawing inputs. Fit physical rows so wrapping cannot exceed assigned height. Keep 80x24 defaults for unavailable/zero dimensions and supported-width behavior.

Working status requirements verbatim: 'Whenever the existing live working line is drawn, including Thinking, Writing and other phases using that same component, draw exactly one explicit blank row immediately above and one immediately below it in the normal layout. These are dedicated rows, not an accidental blank last transcript line or top input border. They are not text padding inside the status line.' 'Reserve both rows in the allocation result. When no live working line exists, reserve and draw neither the line nor its gaps. Phase changes must not make the region jump in height. Gaps may collapse under height pressure, but only as a pair (two or zero). They yield before essential input/overlay controls, footer, or a required status row. They must never reintroduce overflow. At 80x24 with an empty prompt and up to four pending items, both gaps must be visible while a turn runs.' Preserve the existing status.running working-line predicate, including non-turn phases using it.

Use pendingPreviewLines() with exactly the allocated combined budget; the summary is inside that budget. 'Settling a hidden steer and draining a hidden queued item must update the summary correctly. Pending content returns to the preview when space becomes available. Existing plain return and Ctrl-S behavior is unchanged.' Do not alter the send/drain/applied-promise code paths to achieve fitting.

Diagnostic and state policy verbatim: 'If the essential set still exceeds usable rows after the optional regions yield, replace the interactive frame with a height-bounded `Terminal too small — enlarge to continue` diagnostic (clipped to the supported width). This applies to any undersized input or overlay, not just a fixed terminal-height threshold. All surface bounds become inactive in this mode; do not clip an actionable overlay and leave its handlers running.' 'In the diagnostic fallback, do not accept draft edits, submits, menu choices, approval answers or mouse actions on hidden surfaces. Preserve their state. Keep the existing Ctrl-C cancel/quit path available, including its existing confirmation semantics, and keep host events/resize subscriptions alive. Do not cancel a turn, dismiss an ask, lose a draft/history, or resolve a queued item merely because the terminal shrank. On expansion, restore the current surface and state. Existing externally driven ask expiry remains unchanged.'

'Input/answer drafts, pending messages, menu/picker state and transcript scroll/follow state must survive a temporary zero-height viewport or diagnostic fallback. Existing behavior for new messages and explicit scroll-to-bottom remains unchanged. Do not remount the entire chat session just to recover drawing.' 'Never mount a viewport that internally forces a one-row minimum when allocated zero.' Implement a narrow state-preserving suspension path: adapt TranscriptViewport to draw no rows at zero without discarding memory, and preserve local picker/slash/ask selection ownership through hidden rendering or narrowly lifted state. Do not reset query, pointer, dismissal, history, follow/scroll memory or per-request answers on a resize. Hidden content must consume no physical rows. Gate mounted surface handlers with returned visibility now; US-004 completes shared key-time claims, screen shortcuts and mouse geometry.

**Scope** — In: ChatApp measurement/allocation/render wiring, slash/mention desired-row versus allocated-view integration, explicit status-gap rows, compact header and combined previews, diagnostic presentation, zero-viewport/surface state lifetime and direct surface activation props, mounted frame/state regressions. Out: final shared event-time key/mouse ownership, footer hit-test plumbing and renderer-boundary recovery (US-004); queue draining, changes to accepted/discarded steering behavior, and broad ChatApp refactoring.

**Interface** — Consume allocateChatFrame() and its immutable surface/region geometry from US-002. Pass those sizes, render caps and visibility to existing components rather than letting children increase budgets. Retain session identity and existing host/ask contracts; no new user configuration or persisted-data migration.

**Test strategy detail** — Add concern-based mounted frame and suspension suites, extracting existing describe blocks if needed because chat-app-layout is near its hard line limit. Assert physical row counts at H=1,4,5,8,9,10,12,24,40, not merely footer presence. Include 17/40 unresolved steers at 80x24, four queued messages at 80x12, actual long hints/drafts, overlays and the explicit gap neighbors/phase transition/end. Shrink/expand nonempty drafts, answer drafts, scroll/follow, filtered picker query/selection and slash/mention selection/dismissal state without a session remount. Update obsolete tests that explicitly bless height-five overflow. Keep mandatory mounted assertions independent of PTY support; reuse mountChatPicker and fake clocks.
acceptanceCriteria: When ChatApp is mounted at H=2,3,4,5,8,9,10,12,24 or 40 across idle/busy input with short/long drafts, slash/mention menus, queue-only/steer-only/mixed pending items, asks and pickers, then its physical frame contains no more than H - 1 rows as measured from complete frame row counts, not footer-string presence.
When ChatApp is mounted at H=1, then it draws at most one clipped non-interactive diagnostic row without scrolling output.
When terminal dimensions are unavailable or zero, then ChatApp uses the existing 80-column and 24-row fallbacks for the unavailable dimensions.
When an idle full-height 80x24 chat has an empty prompt and no overlay, then its frame retains the existing three-row header, transcript, framed input and footer composition within 23 rows.
When 17 or 40 accepted steers remain unresolved at 80x24, then ChatApp's physical frame contains at most 23 rows.
When four queued messages wait at 80x12, then ChatApp's physical frame contains at most 11 rows.
When a turn runs at 80x24 with an empty prompt and zero through four pending items, then one dedicated blank row is drawn immediately above and one immediately below the live working line.
When the live phase changes from Thinking to Writing or another phase using the same component, then the status region retains its allocated height.
When the live working line ends, then ChatApp removes the status row and both dedicated gaps.
When height pressure removes the optional working gaps, then ChatApp draws neither gap while retaining the required live status row in interactive mode.
When ask or picker replaces input, then hidden queue/steer previews consume no rows.
When a steer hidden by the preview budget settles and overflow remains, then the drawn '+N pending' count equals all remaining pending items minus individually shown previews.

When a queued item hidden by the preview budget drains through the existing send path and overflow remains, then the drawn '+N pending' count equals all remaining pending items minus individually shown previews.
When space becomes available after previews were hidden, then the current pending projection reappears in preserved send/steer order.
When an essential input or overlay minimum cannot fit, then ChatApp replaces the entire interactive composition with 'Terminal too small — enlarge to continue' clipped to the supported width.
When transcript allocation reaches zero, then TranscriptViewport contributes zero physical rows without an internally forced one-row minimum.
When an idle input or running-turn input shrinks into diagnostic and expands, then its nonempty draft and history are preserved.
When a question ask shrinks into diagnostic and expands, then its nonempty answer draft is preserved for the same request.
When a chat shrinks into diagnostic and expands, then pending queue and steering content remain preserved without resize-induced settlement or reordering.
When a picker shrinks into diagnostic and expands, then its query and selection are preserved.
When a slash menu or mention menu temporarily has no drawn rows or enters diagnostic and returns, then its query, selection and dismissal state are preserved.

Given unchanged slash/mention query and matches, when the terminal shrinks and returns to its original dimensions, then the menu draws its pre-shrink row count rather than retaining a degraded desired count.

When a scrolled transcript temporarily has zero viewport height or enters diagnostic and returns, then its scroll/follow state is preserved, retaining existing behavior for new messages and explicit scroll-to-bottom.
When resize alone enters diagnostic, then it neither cancels a turn nor dismisses a pending ask.
When a running host emits transcript content during diagnostic and the terminal expands, then the restored transcript includes that content without a chat-session remount.

When the host expires an ask externally during diagnostic and the terminal expands, then the restored surface reflects the current pending ask state rather than redisplaying the expired ask, preserving existing externally driven expiry behavior.
When stdout emits resize during diagnostic, then ChatApp redraws from the newly reported dimensions without a chat-session remount.
When supported-width layouts resize, then their text rows remain within the physical rows assigned by the allocation.

routing.reasoning: Cross-cutting React composition and state-lifetime changes must prevent frame overflow while preserving drafts, queues, overlay selection and viewport memory across zero-height/diagnostic transitions.

userStories.title: Bind interactions and resize recovery to the drawn frame
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Make every key/mouse consumer use drawn allocation bounds and complete physical-terminal resize recovery without disabling incremental rendering globally.

**Motivation** — Checking only whether a footer string appears in lastFrame() is insufficient: the virtual frame can be taller than the terminal.

**Approach** — Thread US-002's allocation through ChatApp, TranscriptViewport/selection, slash/mention controllers, useChatKeys, image attachment and useJobsOpener. Replace hardcoded three-row transcript offsets and terminal-height-derived footer position with actual drawn coordinates. Consume the desired-content versus final allocated-view separation delivered by US-003 in useMentionMenu; bind its event-time claims to that final visibility rather than recreating measurement or letting menuRowsFor create a second allocation. Preserve existing batched-key/ref guards and intersect them with current drawn visibility, surface precedence and control locks. A hidden menu cannot own navigation through a stale acted/ownsKeys hold. Keep normal visible interactions compatible.

The spec requires verbatim: 'Pass geometry and visibility into interaction consumers; do not introduce a second competing layout model. Diagnostic visibility gates every surface handler, including AskCard, Picker, input, slash/mention menus, viewport selection/scrolling, and the jobs opener. This gating must also cover screen-level shortcuts such as Ctrl-S, Ctrl-V and Ctrl-G; only resize, host events and the existing Ctrl-C cancel/quit path remain active in diagnostic mode.' Gate Ctrl-O, Ctrl-B, Ctrl-T, Shift-Tab and Escape as well, not just the named examples; preserve Ctrl-C confirmation/cancel/quit semantics, including confirmation asks, without making a hidden ask answerable. Restore the same visible targets on expansion without resetting their state.

'In the diagnostic fallback, do not accept draft edits, submits, menu choices, approval answers or mouse actions on hidden surfaces. Preserve their state. Keep the existing Ctrl-C cancel/quit path available, including its existing confirmation semantics, and keep host events/resize subscriptions alive.' 'Derive transcript mouse coordinates, selection/click offsets, footer job-strip hit tests and visible menu key claims from the drawn layout. Compact header/zero viewport must not leave hardcoded three-row offsets behind. A hidden surface must not own keys or clicks. Existing normal-layout interactions stay compatible.' Preserve ask > picker > input precedence and current approval option semantics. Do not fix streaming drag-selection cancellation.

Resize recovery requirements verbatim: 'After shrinking and expanding, the complete current frame must be correct: header restored, no ghost Thinking/Writing lines, queue rows or transcript fragments in header/footer space. Re-test with the fitted frame before changing Ink integration. If stale cells persist, implement a scoped resize invalidation/full repaint through the renderer boundary and test it; do not disable incremental rendering for every streaming tick or issue terminal clears from React render. Preserve alternate-screen teardown and terminal restoration.' Reproduce against source renderChat in index.ts after US-003; the existing root Ink patch may already suffice. Do not change it speculatively. Always deliver production interaction/geometry corrections in this story; renderer changes are conditional on the physical reproduction, not an excuse for a test-only story. Any necessary resize listener/invalidation belongs at the renderer lifecycle boundary and must be removed on failure/unmount.

**Scope** — In: allocated key ownership and mouse bounds, diagnostic shortcut freeze, restoration of visible controls, scoped renderer correction only if demonstrated necessary, integrated mounted and real-PTY regressions, root guide for capability-gated PTY execution. Out: component minima (US-001), allocator/projection algorithm (US-002), frame drawing and state ownership already delivered in US-003; streaming drag-selection cancellation (a separate confirmed bug), permission-policy changes and dependency upgrades.

**Interface** — Consume the allocation's returned region top/rows/active-target flags in existing hook/component options. Convert allocator coordinates to terminal 1-based coordinates at the event boundary. Preserve ChatHost/ask contracts and renderChat's Instance teardown API. Keep incrementalRendering enabled outside any demonstrated resize-only invalidation.

**Test strategy detail** — Use strict three-session isolation, since accidentally actionable hidden approvals can authorize unseen choices. Extend existing selection, viewport, jobs-opener, ask/choice, picker, slash/mention, chat-key and index/incremental suites; assert actual host action counts and unchanged state, not just handler props. Separately cover running/idle input, question/approval/choice ask, picker, slash and mention surfaces through tiny fallback and expansion. Exercise Enter, option shortcuts, menu choice/navigation, picker choose/cycle/stop, Ctrl-G, Ctrl-S, Ctrl-V, footer clicks and viewport mouse actions while hidden, then prove the same controls act on restored visible targets. Include normal/compact coordinate tests and precedence tests.

Add a deterministic test-owned real tmux PTY integration fixture that imports source renderChat and a fake host, with no LLM calls. Start a turn, queue four messages, resize 80x24 -> 80x12 -> 80x24, then compare the complete final terminal screen to the expected current frame. Repeat for 17 unresolved steers and a tiny-height diagnostic cycle. Check repeated status ticks and return to idle. Wait for explicit readiness/frame conditions with bounded timeouts, never fragile arbitrary sleeps. Run the local check only when the required PTY/tmux capabilities exist, reporting an explicit skip reason otherwise; document the same command and requirements in docs/guides/chat-layout-pty.md. Unit/mounted row and interaction assertions remain mandatory when PTY is unavailable; do not change coverage floors. In finally clean up only test-owned processes, sessions and unique socket paths on success, timeout and failure. Preserve alternate-screen/mouse/title restoration and existing incremental redraw tests. Run targeted explicit-path tests, then the project's normal pipeline gates; no bare bun test. Do not leave probe processes or unrelated production edits.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a visible viewport whose first row contains transcript content rather than padding or a marker, when transcriptPointAt() receives terminal cell (x, allocatedTop + 1) with x >= 1, then it returns the first drawn transcript line with column x - 1 in both normal and compact layouts.
When transcript viewport allocation is hidden or zero-height, then selection, clicks and scrolling cannot activate transcript actions.
When a footer job strip is clicked in normal or compact layouts, then useJobsOpener targets the strip at the allocated drawn footer row and columns.
When the footer or its strip is hidden, then its mouse cells cannot open jobs or task output.
When a slash or mention menu has no visible allocated rows, then it owns no navigation or choice keys.

When an ask overlays a picker or input, then bottom-surface edit/choice/navigation keys reach the visible ask instead of the hidden picker or input, preserving existing ask > picker > input precedence without suppressing otherwise-supported visible viewport shortcuts.
When a picker overlays input, then hidden input and its menus cannot claim surface keys.
When diagnostic mode receives draft typing or Enter for idle input or running-turn input, then the observable draft/history, pending queue/steers and host.send call record remain unchanged.
When diagnostic mode receives question-answer typing or Enter, then the answer draft and question resolution remain unchanged.
When diagnostic mode receives approval shortcuts or choice keys, then the pending ask and controller decisions remain unchanged.
When diagnostic mode receives slash or mention navigation and choice keys, then menu selection, draft and host actions remain unchanged.
When diagnostic mode receives picker query typing, choice, cycle or stop keys, then picker query/selection and pending effort state remain unchanged.
When diagnostic mode receives picker choice or stop keys, then it invokes no host selection or job/task-stop action.
When diagnostic mode receives footer job-strip clicks or Ctrl-G, then useJobsOpener invokes neither open('jobs') nor showOutput() and leaves picker state unchanged.
When diagnostic mode receives viewport mouse input, then viewport scroll/selection and transcript actions remain unchanged.
When diagnostic mode receives Ctrl-S, then draft, pending messages and steer/send/cancel effects remain unchanged.
When diagnostic mode receives Ctrl-V, then it triggers no clipboard attachment action or draft mutation.
When diagnostic mode receives Ctrl-O, Ctrl-B, Ctrl-T, Shift-Tab or Escape, then it triggers no surface mutation or host action, leaving only Ctrl-C, host events and resize active.
Given a diagnostic-mode running turn with no armed interrupt, when Ctrl-C is pressed, then host.cancel() is invoked once through the established interrupt path.

Given diagnostic mode with an idle turn or an interrupt armed within the existing 2000ms window, when Ctrl-C is pressed, then the established close path consults host.confirmBeforeClose() before host.close() when confirmation is supplied.
When host.confirmBeforeClose() resolves false after diagnostic-mode Ctrl-C, then host.close() is not invoked, preserving existing confirmation semantics.

When each suppressed control is retried after expansion in separate running-input, idle-input, question/approval/choice-ask, picker, slash and mention cases, then its resulting draft/selection, controller invocation or host call matches the same control on an equivalent never-shrunk visible surface.
When an approval option row cannot be fully displayed, then its option or shortcut cannot resolve the ask through a clipped interactive surface.

When source renderChat in a deterministic fake-host PTY runs a turn with four queued messages through 80x24 -> 80x12 -> 80x24, driven by explicit readiness/frame conditions with bounded timeouts rather than arbitrary sleeps and no LLM calls, then the complete final terminal screen matches the expected current frame.
When the same real-PTY resize sequence runs with 17 unresolved steers, then the complete final screen matches the expected bounded current frame.
When source renderChat passes through a tiny-height diagnostic cycle in the real PTY, then expansion restores the complete expected current frame.
When repeated status ticks occur after shrink/expand, then no ghost Thinking/Writing, pending-preview or transcript cells remain in header/footer space.
When the turn returns to idle after resize, then the physical terminal screen matches the current idle frame without stale status content.
When streaming/status ticks occur outside a resize correction, then incremental rendering remains enabled rather than globally repainting every tick.
When only a status tick changes the frame without a resize, then renderer output contains no resize-invalidation or full-screen clear sequence.
When renderChat unmounts after taking a TTY alternate screen, then its teardown emits the existing mouse-disable, alternate-screen-leave and saved-title-restore sequences once.
When the renderer throws during renderChat setup, then alternate-screen restoration and mouse disposal occur before the same error propagates, preserving existing terminal restoration on failure.
When a real-PTY scenario completes or fails, then finally cleanup leaves no test-owned probe process, tmux session or socket path behind and does not affect unrelated processes/sessions.
When PTY/tmux capabilities are unavailable locally, then the real-PTY check reports an explicit skip reason while mandatory pure/mounted assertions remain enabled without lowered coverage floors.
When visible input sends or steers messages after these changes, then plain Return and Ctrl-S retain their existing behavior without queued-message loss.

When Ctrl-S is pressed on an empty visible prompt with queued messages and host.steer accepts, then host.steer receives the oldest queued message exactly once, preserving the existing steer-queued regression behavior.

When the established normal-layout focused layout, input-focus and steer-queued interaction sequences are replayed, then their frame/cursor state and send/steer effects match the established expectations apart from the specified bounds and working-status spacing changes.
When visible approval/choice controls answer an ask after these changes, then controller resolution matches an equivalent never-resized visible ask, preserving existing approval semantics.

When the production-source diff is inspected, then every hunk is confined to chat presentation/allocation, visibility/interaction geometry or a demonstrated resize-only renderer correction, with no production source edits unrelated to this feature.

analysis:
Goal and evidence: this is a presentation/geometry repair, not a chat execution change. The supplied evidence at c0add8c96 reproduces actual renderChat overflow and stale cells through an isolated tmux PTY despite 82 focused tests passing. Preserve branch feat/chat-layout-overflow, plan profile native-codex-dsm and spec reviewer openai-codex/gpt-6-luna. No implementation or tests were executed while drafting this PRD; the exposed tools provide file operations but no shell or codebase-memory MCP, so discovery used direct reads/search rather than the unavailable graph.

Current composition and defects: packages/nax/src/tui/chat/ChatApp.tsx:124 defines a fixed three-row header and :130 forces a one-row viewport. terminalSize at :219 retains 80x24 defaults through unavailable/zero dimensions. At :431 workingShown uses status.running; preserve that predicate rather than replacing it with busy/turnRunning. At :436-452 the screen independently builds queue and steering rows, subtracts them from bottomBudget and floors that budget to one. At :1319 inputBudget is again floored; :1341 measures inputRows without the hint that drawing receives at :1453, while :1342-1351 subtracts bottomRows and floors the viewport again. These independent floors cannot guarantee H-1. Drawing starts at :1353, fixes transcript top to HEADER_ROWS at :1366, mounts an always-positive viewport, draws one unpadded working line, clips overlays without disabling their actions, and renders footer last. Ask > picker > input precedence already exists and must remain. Header path/rule may yield together, then the product row; drawing, mouse offsets and footer coordinates must follow the same allocation.

Pending state and dependencies: packages/nax/src/tui/chat/message-queue.ts:122 projects three queued items plus '+N more'; :143 projects every unresolved steer. Neither shares a height budget. Keep pushQueued (:41), pushDiscardedSteer (:83), takeQueued (:98), queueToPrompt (:108), applied-promise handling and ChatApp send/drain paths unchanged. Add a combined projection in arrival-order steers then oldest-first queue, capped to four total physical rows with '+N pending' inside the budget. Projection must never mutate state or settle promises. ChatApp owns persistent queued/steering state and synchronous refs at :321-378; UI hiding cannot change these owners. Plain Return and Ctrl-S behavior is regression-sensitive, including batched Return and accepted/discarded/unsupported steering paths.

Surface measurement: packages/nax/src/tui/chat/ChatInput.tsx:179 caps text at eight rows, :182 exports two rule rows, :202-240 defines width/container/hint/busy/cap inputs, and inputRows (:349) uses the same visibleRows implementation as rendering. Extend/reuse this pure model to expose minimum and desired dimensions, keeping the actual hint, width, busy flag and drawn text cap identical between measuring and rendering. packages/nax/src/tui/chat/bottom-region.ts:22 defines a three-row input minimum, but bottomRowsFor (:46) clamps overlays to budgets below their real minima and menuRowsFor (:65) performs another independent subtraction. Retire/delegate competing allocation arithmetic after integration; retain useful precedence predicates without a second model. packages/nax/src/tui/chat/AskCard.tsx:203-227 wraps titles/attribution and option labels; fitCard (:306) can discard the entire head while retaining an oversized tail. askCardLayout (:330) forces an answer-box minimum independently of available rows. Measure safe minima at actual width: full title and options for approvals/choices, first question row and three-row answer for questions, countdown/rules and measured wrapped elision marker when body is withheld. Existing labels, attribution and controller decisions must not change. packages/nax/src/tui/chat/Picker.tsx:95 fixedRows includes frame/title, model filter and optional note; pickerRows (:142) can exceed its budget through fixed rows, and visibleEntries (:100) may yield zero for a nonempty list while handlers can still select. Empty filtered lists legitimately need no selected entry, and must not choose/cycle/stop one.

State-lifetime risks: ChatApp owns input draft/history and per-request answer draft at packages/nax/src/tui/chat/ChatApp.tsx:319-328, but AskCard selected option is local at AskCard.tsx:411, Picker selection is local at Picker.tsx:271, SlashMenu selection is local at SlashMenu.tsx:166 and TranscriptViewport memory is local at TranscriptViewport.tsx:212. Conditional unmounting during diagnostic/zero-row layouts would silently reset those values. Preserve the session and surface state owners while suppressing drawing/actions, or narrowly lift only the state that would otherwise be lost. Do not broadly refactor ChatApp. TranscriptViewport.tsx:77 floors height to one, :221 folds changed dimensions/content into memory, :231 subscribes mouse and :253 subscribes scrolling keys. A zero-height allocation must draw nothing and cannot feed an internally forced one-row viewport; preserve scroll/follow state through suspension while retaining normal new-message and explicit-End/followToken behavior. viewport.ts:51-70 currently clamps offset and follows again when clamped to zero, so simply unmounting or rewriting memory on suspension is unsafe.

Interaction geometry: selection.ts:21 translates 1-based terminal cells using geometry.top, and :33 tests the marker row. ChatApp must supply the drawn top rather than three. use-jobs-opener.ts:22 owns FRAME_SLACK_ROWS=1, :42 tests strip columns, :91 computes footerRow from terminal height instead of the drawn region, and :120 owns Ctrl-G and mouse press/release. Feed allocated footer bounds/visibility into it. use-mention-menu.ts:187 computes another menu share with menuRowsFor; separate desired content from final allocated rows, preserving live query/index/pointer refs and key-time claims. Its :278 ownsNavigation hold must not make hidden menus claim keys. use-slash-menu-keys.ts:52 preserves synchronous prompt/dismissal state; SlashMenu.tsx:187 reads ownsKeys at event time. Keep these protections for multiple keys delivered before React redraws, while intersecting claims with the allocation. ChatApp.tsx:535 has ungated screen Ctrl-O/Ctrl-V/Ctrl-S and escape; useChatKeys.ts:173 owns Ctrl-C, Ctrl-B, Ctrl-T and Shift-Tab. Diagnostic mode must block all surface/screen shortcuts except the existing Ctrl-C cancel/quit path, without disabling host events, expiry or resize. Gating an approval's display/action availability is not a permission policy change; do not touch permission resolution or the host's ask decisions.

Renderer boundary: packages/nax/src/tui/chat/index.ts:66 mounts the actual alternate-screen chat, :117 restores title/mouse/screen idempotently, :125 renders with incrementalRendering:true at :138 and :151 wraps unmount restoration. patches/ink@6.7.0.patch:1-13 already repairs incremental cursor origin by using previousLines.length-1. First fit frames, then reproduce shrink/expand through this actual source entry. Change renderer invalidation only if stale cells persist; if necessary, scope a full repaint to resize, never every status/stream tick and never a clear from React render. Any listener/timer must be cleaned up through existing _deps/lifecycle seams. No dependency upgrade is needed or allowed.

Tests and verification: existing mandatory pure suites include test/unit/tui/chat/bottom-region.test.ts, message-queue.test.ts, selection.test.ts, use-jobs-opener.test.ts and viewport.test.ts. Existing UI suites include test/ui/chat/chat-app-layout.test.tsx (779 lines, nearly the 800-line hard limit), chat-input.test.tsx, chat-input-focus.test.tsx, ask-card.test.tsx, choice-card.test.tsx, picker.test.tsx, slash-menu.test.tsx, chat-mention-picker.test.tsx, transcript-viewport.test.tsx, jobs-opener.test.tsx, chat-steer-queued.test.tsx and chat-steering.test.tsx. chat-app-layout.test.tsx:153 already demonstrates stdout resize through act; :262 and :428 explicitly permit overflow at height five and must be replaced with the new bounded behavior, not retained as compatibility requirements. Existing normal-width/cursor/ask semantics are regression anchors. test/helpers/chat-picker.tsx:73 exports the shared mounted fake as mountChatPicker, with event/send gates; reuse/extend it through @test/helpers and reuse fake clocks rather than duplicating host scaffolding. Existing ink-incremental-render.test.tsx:21 spawns a non-PTY fixture and :40 asserts cursor escape output; it cannot prove a final physical terminal screen after resize. No reusable real-PTY resize harness was established by the targeted search. Add a test-owned deterministic tmux PTY fixture using source renderChat and a fake host with no LLM calls, explicit readiness/frame conditions, bounded timeouts, final-screen comparison and finally cleanup limited to its own session/socket/processes. Capability skips need explicit reasons and root docs instructions; mandatory unit/mounted frame assertions cannot be skipped or coverage floors lowered.

Implementation order and migration: first make existing component measurement/drawing agree on safe minimum/desired sizes; second introduce one pure frame allocation result plus combined pending projection; third replace ChatApp arithmetic and implement state-preserving bounded rendering; fourth route interaction bounds/key ownership through that result and verify physical resize recovery, adding only a demonstrated renderer correction. These are internal APIs with no persisted-data, configuration, dependency or public host contract migration. Remove/delegate obsolete height arithmetic once consumers move; do not maintain parallel models. Follow root and packages/nax AGENTS, docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md and canonical .nax/rules. Use existing component layout helpers, Bun-native external operations via injectable seams, named constants and narrowly scoped helpers. Keep new tests beside the affected modules; split large suites by concern rather than bug number. Run targeted explicit-path bun tests (for example from packages/nax: bun test test/unit/tui/chat/frame-layout.test.ts --timeout=30000 and relevant test/ui/chat paths), then the normal package/pipeline gates, never bare bun test or bun run nax. Pipeline runs typecheck/lint/tests in nax sessions; outside a session use package typecheck/check:all and normal test runner.
